finding: 6-month holdout (May-Oct 2025) gross profit: actual ₹51.2 L. Customer-base simulation forecast ₹46.0 L (-10%, median of 6-month totals) using a 12-month history window. Every window under-forecast this period (12m -10%, 18m -13%, 24m -8%), so the model is mildly conservative; the actual total sat inside the 80% interval. Best monthly MAE: Exp. smoothing (SES) (₹1.6 L/month). Monthly errors are large for every method (noise ~41% CV); totals over 6+ months are reliable, single months are not.

Scenario A (no new sign-ups): 2026 gross profit ₹96.9 L (80% range ₹79.9 L–₹115.4 L), net sales ₹358.8 L. Scenario B (sign-ups resume): ₹107.8 L. For reference 2025 Jan-Oct actual was ₹83.6 L (about ₹100.3 L annualised).

2026 revenue orders, median: A 132, B 148, C 152 (2025 annualised ≈ 137). About 11.2 customers order in a typical month under A. The base keeps growing slowly because the existing 220 buyers keep repeating.

Nov 2025–Dec 2026 new buyers, median: A 27, B 41, C 43. Under A the unconverted pool drains to about 53 and 84% of 2026 orders are repeat orders. Without new sign-ups the business becomes almost purely a repeat business.

Expected 2025 full-year PPAC ≈ ₹99,350, so the 2026 target (+5%) is ≈ ₹104,317. Forecast 2026 PPAC under A: ₹92,247 (P10–P90 ₹74,501–₹113,821); probability of hitting target: A 24%, B 20%, C 22%. PPAC is a ratio, so it barely moves with acquisition scenarios; it moves with order frequency, order value and margin.

2026 units (scenario A, median): Beauty 159, Electronics 129, Fashion 114, Home & Kitchen 113, Sports 144. Roughly 165 units per quarter in total. Comparison with stock is not possible: stock_quantity is a static snapshot unrelated to sales (audit Q15).
Cancel/return rate posterior mean 4.9%. 2026 Q1: median 1 lost orders (P10–P90 0–3), ≈ ₹0.7 L profit forgone. Too few events to model drivers; track the rate monthly against ~5%.
